questions.prompt: A partner supports the other option in the familiar group decision. Ask one relevant clarification, then give your response to their actual reason.
questions.context:
Your group must choose a meeting today or tomorrow. Your partner prefers today so a new member can attend; you prefer tomorrow so another partner can attend. No date allows everyone to come. Ask which member can attend today, respond to that reason, and propose a next step without claiming full agreement.
Familiar meanings available: member; companion; pal; personally; in person; explanation; to explain.
questions.label: Take your speaking turn

rubric.text: My clarification targets the partner’s stated reason.
My response addresses that reason without inventing a stronger claim.

questions.prompt: Write a structured account of the familiar shared decision for an absent member. Include the reason and a conclusion supported by it.
questions.context:
Two members proposed today because their partner could attend; another proposed tomorrow because a different partner could attend. The group finally agreed on tomorrow and agreed to explain the discussion personally to the absent member. Write that decision and reason; one member still prefers today.
Familiar meanings available: member; companion; pal; thus; consequently; but; however.
questions.label: Write your own message

rubric.text: The issue, reason and conclusion connect coherently.
I distinguished the shared decision from an individual preference.
